source.exp: Luna 9 made the first successful soft landing on the Moon in February 1966. Luna 2 had reached the Moon earlier in 1959, but it impacted the surface rather than performing a survivable landing.

source.exp: ESA is an intergovernmental space organisation headquartered in Paris and established in 1975. Slovenia became a full member on 1 January 2025, taking ESA to 23 Member States.

source.q: What is NISAR and what is its current status?

source.exp: NISAR is the NASA–ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar mission, using complementary L- and S-band radars for global Earth observation. It launched on 30 July 2025 into a 743-km Sun-synchronous orbit and entered its science phase later in 2025.

edits.after: Ariane-1 (V-3)

source.q: When was the APPLE satellite launched, and from where?
source.a: 19 June 1981 — Kourou, French Guiana, on Ariane-1 (V-3)

source.a: PSLV-D1 flew on 20 September 1993 but was unsuccessful; PSLV-D2 succeeded on 15 October 1994; PSLV is a four-stage workhorse used especially for LEO/SSO missions
source.exp: PSLV's first developmental flight, PSLV-D1, took place on 20 September 1993 and did not achieve the intended orbit. PSLV-D2 succeeded on 15 October 1994; the four-stage PSLV later became ISRO's highly reliable workhorse for polar, Sun-synchronous and other Earth orbits.

source.a: GSLV Mk II first flew on 18 April 2001 and can place about 2.25 t into GTO; LVM3 is the separate heavier launcher with over 4 t GTO capability
source.exp: GSLV Mk II is a three-stage launcher whose first developmental flight was on 18 April 2001; its current GTO capability is about 2.25 tonnes. source.a: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish; the General Assembly and Security Council use all six as official and working languages
source.exp: The UN has six official languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish. In the General Assembly and Security Council, all six are also working languages; language practice in the Secretariat is governed separately.

source.a: 1946; New York; UNICEF works in more than 190 countries and territories
source.exp: UNICEF was created in 1946 and is headquartered in New York. It is a UN fund, not a membership organization like the UN itself, so “190 members” is inaccurate; UNICEF works in more than 190 countries and territories.

source.a: UN Tourism; 1975; Madrid, Spain

source.a: EEC Treaty signed 1957 and effective 1958; EU formally created in 1993; 27 member states

source.exp: NAM’s first summit was held in Belgrade in 1961. The five leaders commonly associated with its founding are Jawaharlal Nehru, Sukarno, Josip Broz Tito, Gamal Abdel Nasser and Kwame Nkrumah. NAM currently lists 121 member countries.

source.a: A large geographic area connecting networks across regions, countries or continents
source.exp: A Wide Area Network connects networks over large geographic distances. The Internet is the largest example; a WAN has no fixed maximum of 1000 km and no single standard speed.

edits.before: WAN uses High Level Data Link Control (HDLC) protocol.
edits.after: HDLC is a data-link protocol used on particular links; it does not define every WAN.

source.q: What does HDLC stand for, and where is it used?
source.a: High-Level Data Link Control — a bit-oriented data-link protocol used on serial/point-to-point links
source.exp: HDLC is a data-link-layer protocol standardized for bit-oriented communication over serial links. It can be used in WAN environments, but modern WANs do not universally use one protocol.

edits.before: creates secure, encrypted connection between device and internet
edits.after: creates an encrypted tunnel between endpoints; it does not guarantee complete anonymity

source.q: What does a VPN do?
source.a: Creates an encrypted tunnel between endpoints across an untrusted network such as the Internet
source.exp: A VPN protects traffic by creating a logical encrypted tunnel. It may connect a user device to a VPN server or connect two networks site-to-site; it is not simply a speed-boosting connection to the Internet.

edits.before: connects millions of mobile and personal computers via network
edits.after: on-demand access to shared computing resources and services over a network

source.q: What is Cloud Computing?
source.a: On-demand delivery of shared computing resources and services over a network, usually the Internet
source.exp: Cloud computing provides resources such as servers, storage, databases and software on demand over networks. It is a service model, not merely the act of connecting millions of personal computers.

edits.after: Google, Bing, Yahoo and DuckDuckGo

source.a: Malware that attaches to a host file/program and replicates when the infected host executes
source.exp: A computer virus typically needs a host file or program and spreads when that host is executed. Some viruses damage data or software, but damage is not the defining feature.

source.a: Requires two different authentication factors, such as a password plus a one-time code or biometric
source.exp: Two-factor authentication combines two independent factor categories, such as something you know (password), have (phone/security key), or are (biometric). Two steps of the same factor type do not necessarily constitute true 2FA.

source.exp: T.H. “Vikku” Vinayakram is a celebrated Carnatic ghatam artist. The ghatam is a clay pot played by striking its body and mouth with the hands; the pot itself vibrates, placing it among solid-body ghana instruments rather than membrane drums.

source.a: Manipur’s Meitei cultural traditions; Vaishnavism and Radha-Krishna devotion
source.exp: Manipuri developed in Manipur, drawing on Meitei ritual traditions as well as later Vaishnava devotion. Its Ras dances portray Radha and Krishna, but the wider repertoire also includes Lai Haraoba and percussion dances; a language is not the geographical origin of a dance.

edits.before: Reign of Bhagyachandra and Keerti Chandra
edits.after: King Bhagyachandra shaped the eighteenth-century Manipuri Ras tradition

source.q: Which eighteenth-century king shaped Manipuri Ras, and which older ritual tradition predates its Vaishnava development?
source.a: King Bhagyachandra; Lai Haraoba
source.exp: King Bhagyachandra was central to the eighteenth-century development of Manipuri Ras, including its costume and performance traditions. Lai Haraoba is an older Meitei ritual festival with dance, predating the Vaishnava Ras repertoire; the two represent related but distinct historical layers.

edits.after: 2000, by the Sangeet Natak Akademi

source.q: What is the origin of Sattriya, and when was it recognized as a classical dance?
source.a: Vaishnava sattras of Assam; recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000
source.exp: Sattriya developed in Assam’s Vaishnava sattras and was recognised as a classical dance by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000. Its monastic roots are important, but contemporary training and performance also take place outside monasteries and include women.

edits.after: Chhau has a separate UNESCO intangible-heritage inscription

source.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes the standard eight classical dance forms from Chhau’s UNESCO inscription?
source.a: The standard list contains eight; Chhau’s intangible-heritage inscription is a separate recognition, not automatic proof of a ninth classical form
source.exp: The standard eight are Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Odissi and Sattriya. Chhau is a major eastern Indian dance tradition inscribed as UNESCO intangible heritage in 2010; international heritage listing and domestic classical-dance classification are different systems.

edits.before: Andhra PradeshGhanta Mardala, Veeranatyam, Dhimsa, Butta Bommalu, Lambadi, Kolattam
edits.after: Andhra PradeshVeeranatyam, Dhimsa, Lambadi and Kolattam

source.q: Which of the following are folk dances of Andhra Pradesh?
source.a: Veeranatyam, Dhimsa, Lambadi and Kolattam
source.exp: Andhra Pradesh is associated with Veeranatyam, Dhimsa, Lambadi and Kolattam. Dhimsa is a community dance associated with the Araku region; Veeranatyam has a Shaiva ritual context, while Kolattam uses sticks. These traditions are not all exclusive to one state.

edits.after: AssamBihu, Bagurumba, Bhortal and Jhumur

source.q: Which of the following are folk dances of Assam?
source.a: Bihu, Bagurumba, Bhortal and Jhumur
source.exp: Assam is associated with Bihu, Bagurumba, Bhortal and Jhumur. Bihu is associated with seasonal celebrations, Bagurumba with the Bodo community, and Bhortal with cymbals. Jhumur is also performed by tea-garden communities and has related traditions outside Assam.

edits.before: BiharKamla, Chhau, Birha, Jat-Jatin, Soharai, Jijhiya/Jhijhiya, Sama-Chakeva, Videsiya (Bhikhari Thakur)
edits.after: BiharJat-Jatin, Jhijhiya, Bidesia and Sama-Chakeva

source.q: Which group of traditional performing arts or dance-related festivities is associated with Bihar?
source.a: Jat-Jatin, Jhijhiya, Bidesia and Sama-Chakeva
source.exp: Bihar is associated with Jat-Jatin, Jhijhiya, Bidesia and Sama-Chakeva. Bihar’s traditions include Jat-Jatin dance-song, Jhijhiya dance, Bidesia folk theatre and the Sama-Chakeva festival arts of Mithila. These are different performing or festive genres, not four interchangeable dance names.

edits.before: ChhattisgarhPandwani, Sua Karma, Gaur Maria, Raut Nacha, Saila, Sarhul Bar, Nacha
edits.after: ChhattisgarhPandavani, Sua, Karma, Gaur Maria, Raut Nacha and Saila

source.q: Which group of traditional performing arts or dance-related festivities is associated with Chhattisgarh?
source.a: Pandavani, Sua, Karma, Gaur Maria, Raut Nacha and Saila
source.exp: Chhattisgarh is associated with Pandavani, Sua, Karma, Gaur Maria, Raut Nacha and Saila. Pandavani narrates episodes of the Mahabharata through singing and enactment; it is not simply a folk dance. Sua, Raut Nacha and other community dances form part of Chhattisgarh’s varied performing heritage.

edits.after: GoaFugdi, Ghode Modni, Mando and Tarangmel

source.q: Which group of traditional performing arts or dance-related festivities is associated with Goa?
source.a: Fugdi, Ghode Modni, Mando and Tarangmel
source.exp: Goa is associated with Fugdi, Ghode Modni, Mando and Tarangmel. Fugdi is commonly performed by women, Ghode Modni uses horse representations, and Tarangmel is a procession-based dance. Mando is a distinctive Goan song-and-dance genre, often expressing love and social themes.

edits.before: GujaratGarba, Dandiya Raas, Tippani, Rathwa, Dhamal, Gof, Hallisaka
edits.after: GujaratGarba, Dandiya Raas, Tippani, Rathwa dances and Siddi Dhamal

source.q: Which of the following are folk dances of Gujarat?
source.a: Garba, Dandiya Raas, Tippani, Rathwa dances and Siddi Dhamal
source.exp: Gujarat is associated with Garba, Dandiya Raas, Tippani, Rathwa dances and Siddi Dhamal. Garba is a circular devotional dance closely associated with Navratri, while Dandiya Raas uses sticks. Tippani and the dances of Rathwa and Siddi communities illustrate Gujarat’s regional and community diversity; Dhamal also has forms elsewhere.

edits.before: Himachal PradeshNoti (Guinness World Record), Dhurehi, Jhora, Charba, Kulvi Nati, Shon
edits.after: Himachal PradeshNati, Kullu Nati, Dangi and Dandras

source.q: Which of the following are folk dances of Himachal Pradesh?
source.a: Nati, Kullu Nati, Dangi and Dandras
source.exp: Himachal Pradesh is associated with Nati, Kullu Nati, Dangi and Dandras. Nati is a broad family of group dances in Himachal Pradesh, including Kullu Nati. Dangi and Dandras are associated with the Gaddi traditions of Chamba; a participation record belongs to a particular event, not to every performance of Nati.

edits.before: Jammu & KashmirRauf, Hikat, Bhairava Geet, Chakri, Tamali
edits.after: Jammu & KashmirRouf, Hikat, Dumhal and Chakri

source.q: Which group of traditional performing arts or dance-related festivities is associated with Jammu & Kashmir?
source.a: Rouf, Hikat, Dumhal and Chakri
source.exp: Jammu & Kashmir is associated with Rouf, Hikat, Dumhal and Chakri. Rouf and Hikat are associated with Kashmiri dance traditions, while Dumhal is performed in distinctive costumes. Chakri is chiefly a folk singing form; Jammu and Kashmir’s musical and dance traditions should not all be classified as dance alone.

edits.after: JharkhandSeraikella Chhau, Jhumar and Paika

source.q: Which of the following are folk dances of Jharkhand?
source.a: Seraikella Chhau, Jhumar and Paika
source.exp: Jharkhand is associated with Seraikella Chhau, Jhumar and Paika. Seraikella Chhau is Jharkhand’s masked Chhau style, while Jhumar is a regional song-dance tradition and Paika has martial features. Chhau also has major styles in Odisha and West Bengal; its heritage is not exclusive to Jharkhand.

edits.before: KarnatakaBhoota Kola, Yakshagana, Veeragase, Kamsale, Karga, Pata Kunitha, Dollu Kunitha
edits.after: KarnatakaBhoota Kola, Yakshagana, Veeragase and Dollu Kunitha

source.q: Which group of traditional performing arts or dance-related festivities is associated with Karnataka?
source.a: Bhoota Kola, Yakshagana, Veeragase and Dollu Kunitha
source.exp: Karnataka is associated with Bhoota Kola, Yakshagana, Veeragase and Dollu Kunitha. Bhoota Kola is a spirit-related ritual performance, Yakshagana is dance-theatre, Veeragase is a vigorous Shaiva dance, and Dollu Kunitha uses large drums. Their shared Karnataka association does not make them the same genre.

edits.before: KeralaKoikottikali, Kaliyattam, Thappattikkali, Chavittunatakam, Mudiyettu, Chakyar Koothu (UNESCO 2010)
edits.after: KeralaKaikottikali, Chavittunatakam, Mudiyettu and Chakyar Koothu

source.q: Which group of traditional performing arts or dance-related festivities is associated with Kerala?
source.a: Kaikottikali, Chavittunatakam, Mudiyettu and Chakyar Koothu
source.exp: Kerala is associated with Kaikottikali, Chavittunatakam, Mudiyettu and Chakyar Koothu. Kaikottikali is a group dance, Chavittunatakam is theatre with emphatic foot-stamping, and Chakyar Koothu is a narrative performance. Mudiyettu’s Kali–Darika ritual dance-drama was inscribed as UNESCO intangible heritage in 2010; that inscription does not apply to this entire list.

edits.before: Madhya PradeshKarma Dance, Rai Dance, Jawara Dance, Matki Dance
edits.after: Madhya PradeshKarma, Rai, Jawara and Matki dances

source.q: Which of the following are folk dances of Madhya Pradesh?
source.a: Karma, Rai, Jawara and Matki dances
source.exp: Madhya Pradesh is associated with Karma, Rai, Jawara and Matki dances. Rai is strongly associated with Bundelkhand, while Matki is a pot-balancing dance of Malwa. Jawara has ritual associations and Karma is shared with other central and eastern Indian communities; regional boundaries do not contain every folk tradition.

edits.before: MaharashtraTamasha, Lavani, Dhangari Gaja, Lezim, Gafa, Dashavatar
edits.after: MaharashtraTamasha, Lavani, Dhangari Gaja, Lezim and Dashavatar

source.q: Which group of traditional performing arts or dance-related festivities is associated with Maharashtra?
source.a: Tamasha, Lavani, Dhangari Gaja, Lezim and Dashavatar
source.exp: Maharashtra is associated with Tamasha, Lavani, Dhangari Gaja, Lezim and Dashavatar. Lavani combines rhythmic singing and performance; Tamasha and coastal Dashavatar are theatrical traditions. Dhangari Gaja is associated with shepherd communities, while Lezim features rhythmic movement with jingling implements.

edits.before: ManipurThabal Chongba, Basanta Ras, Lai Haraoba, Natras, Nupa Pala
edits.after: ManipurThabal Chongba, Basanta Ras and Lai Haraoba

source.q: Which group of traditional performing arts or dance-related festivities is associated with Manipur?
source.a: Thabal Chongba, Basanta Ras and Lai Haraoba
source.exp: Manipur is associated with Thabal Chongba, Basanta Ras and Lai Haraoba. Thabal Chongba is a community dance associated with Yaoshang festivities, and Lai Haraoba preserves Meitei ritual dance. Basanta Ras belongs to the classical Manipuri Ras repertoire, so this is a list of traditional dance forms rather than exclusively folk dances.

edits.before: MeghalayaPomblang Nongkrem, Shad Suk Mynsiem, Wangala, Laho
edits.after: MeghalayaNongkrem, Shad Suk Mynsiem and Wangala dance festivals

source.q: Which group of traditional performing arts or dance-related festivities is associated with Meghalaya?
source.a: Nongkrem, Shad Suk Mynsiem and Wangala dance festivals
source.exp: Meghalaya is associated with Nongkrem, Shad Suk Mynsiem and Wangala dance festivals. Nongkrem and Shad Suk Mynsiem belong to Khasi cultural traditions, while Wangala is a Garo harvest festival with drumming and dance. These names designate festivals or festival dances, not one uniform tribal dance.

edits.after: MizoramCheraw, Par Lam and Chheihlam

source.q: Which of the following are folk dances of Mizoram?
source.a: Cheraw, Par Lam and Chheihlam
source.exp: Mizoram is associated with Cheraw, Par Lam and Chheihlam. Cheraw is the bamboo dance in which dancers step between rhythmically moved bamboo poles. Par Lam and Chheihlam are other Mizo dance traditions; the bamboo-pole feature distinguishes Cheraw from dances merely performed to drum accompaniment.

edits.before: NagalandZeliang, Rangma, Aaluyattu, Chang Lo, Kuki Dance
edits.after: NagalandZeliang dances, Rengma dances and Chang Lo

source.q: Which of the following are folk dances of Nagaland?
source.a: Zeliang dances, Rengma dances and Chang Lo
source.exp: Nagaland is associated with Zeliang dances, Rengma dances and Chang Lo. Nagaland has distinct dance traditions among its many Naga communities, including Zeliang, Rengma and Chang groups. Some names identify the community rather than a single choreography; themes include agriculture, celebration and martial memory.

edits.before: OdishaRasa Leela, Paika, Goti Pua, Danda Nrutya, Mahari, Danda Yatra, Dalkhai
edits.after: OdishaRasa Leela, Paika, Gotipua, Mahari and Dalkhai

source.q: Which group of traditional performing arts or dance-related festivities is associated with Odisha?
source.a: Rasa Leela, Paika, Gotipua, Mahari and Dalkhai
source.exp: Odisha is associated with Rasa Leela, Paika, Gotipua, Mahari and Dalkhai. Dalkhai is strongly associated with western Odisha; Paika incorporates martial movement. Gotipua and temple Mahari traditions contributed to Odissi, while Rasa Leela is devotional theatre, so these are related performing traditions rather than only folk dances.

edits.after: PunjabGiddha, Bhangra, Jhumar and Gatka

source.q: Which group of traditional performing arts or dance-related festivities is associated with Punjab?
source.a: Giddha, Bhangra, Jhumar and Gatka
source.exp: Punjab is associated with Giddha, Bhangra, Jhumar and Gatka. Giddha and Bhangra are major Punjabi folk dances, and Punjabi Jhumar is another regional form. Gatka is a martial tradition using weapons, not simply a folk dance; the list therefore includes dance and martial performing traditions.

edits.before: RajasthanRauf, Ghoomar, Gair, Bhavai, Chari, Kathputli, Kalbelia (UNESCO 2010), Kachhi Ghodi, Gangaur, Terah Tali
edits.after: RajasthanGhoomar, Gair, Bhavai, Kathputli, Kalbelia and Gangaur festivities

source.q: Which group of traditional performing arts or dance-related festivities is associated with Rajasthan?
source.a: Ghoomar, Gair, Bhavai, Kathputli, Kalbelia and Gangaur festivities
source.exp: Rajasthan is associated with Ghoomar, Gair, Bhavai, Kathputli, Kalbelia and Gangaur festivities. Rajasthan’s Ghoomar, Gair and balancing-based Bhavai are dance forms, while Kathputli is puppetry and Gangaur is a festival. Kalbelia folk songs and dances were inscribed as UNESCO intangible heritage in 2010; this does not classify all listed traditions as dances.

edits.after: SikkimChu-Faat and Bhutia community dances

source.q: Which of the following are folk dances of Sikkim?
source.a: Chu-Faat and Bhutia community dances
source.exp: Sikkim is associated with Chu-Faat and Bhutia community dances. Chu-Faat is a Lepcha group dance honouring Mount Khangchendzonga. Sikkim’s Bhutia, Lepcha and Nepali communities have different dance traditions; “Bhutia dance” is a broad community label rather than the name of just one standard item.

edits.after: Tamil NaduKummi, Kavadi, Kolattam and Karagam

source.q: Which of the following are folk dances of Tamil Nadu?
source.a: Kummi, Kavadi, Kolattam and Karagam
source.exp: Tamil Nadu is associated with Kummi, Kavadi, Kolattam and Karagam. Kummi uses rhythmic clapping, Kolattam uses sticks, and Karagam involves balancing decorated pots. Kavadi performance is linked to Murugan devotion; these folk and ritual forms are distinct from Tamil Nadu’s classical Bharatanatyam.

edits.after: TripuraHojagiri, Mamita and Lebang Boomani

source.q: Which of the following are folk dances of Tripura?
source.a: Hojagiri, Mamita and Lebang Boomani
source.exp: Tripura is associated with Hojagiri, Mamita and Lebang Boomani. Hojagiri is especially associated with the Reang/Bru community and intricate balancing movements. Mamita and Lebang Boomani relate to agricultural life and seasonal celebrations, reflecting Tripura’s varied community traditions.

edits.after: UttarakhandChholiya, Chhapeli, Langvir and Jagar

source.q: Which group of traditional performing arts or dance-related festivities is associated with Uttarakhand?
source.a: Chholiya, Chhapeli, Langvir and Jagar
source.exp: Uttarakhand is associated with Chholiya, Chhapeli, Langvir and Jagar. Chholiya is a sword-dance tradition of Kumaon, Chhapeli is a paired dance, and Langvir involves acrobatic performance. Jagar is ritual invocation through singing and music, sometimes with embodied performance; “Kumaoni” alone is a regional adjective, not one dance title.

edits.before: West BengalKathi, Brita, Chhau, Baul, Alkap, Kirtan, Jatra, Gambhira
edits.after: West BengalKathi, Purulia Chhau, Baul, Kirtan and Jatra

source.q: Which group of traditional performing arts or dance-related festivities is associated with West Bengal?
source.a: Kathi, Purulia Chhau, Baul, Kirtan and Jatra
source.exp: West Bengal is associated with Kathi, Purulia Chhau, Baul, Kirtan and Jatra. Purulia Chhau is a masked dance-drama and Kathi uses sticks. Baul is a spiritual music tradition, Kirtan is devotional singing and Jatra is theatre; treating this entire Bengal list as folk dance would erase important genre distinctions.

edits.before: HaryanaJhumar, Phag, Dhamal, Luru, Gugga, Khoria, Gagor
edits.after: HaryanaJhumar, Phag, Dhamal and Loor

source.q: Which of the following are folk dances of Haryana?
source.a: Jhumar, Phag, Dhamal and Loor
source.exp: Haryana is associated with Jhumar, Phag, Dhamal and Loor. Phag is associated with spring and Holi, Dhamal with energetic group movement, and Loor with women’s seasonal performance. Similar names such as Jhumar occur in other regions too; the local Haryanvi style provides the relevant association.

edits.after: LadakhShondol and Jabro

source.q: Which of the following are folk dances of Ladakh?
source.a: Shondol and Jabro
source.exp: Ladakh is associated with Shondol and Jabro. Shondol is associated with Ladakh’s courtly dance heritage, while Jabro is a community dance of the Changthang region. Ladakh also has monastic masked dances; a regional or community term such as Balti does not by itself identify one specific choreography.

edits.after: Andaman & NicobarNicobari community dance

source.q: Which option identifies an indigenous community dance tradition of the Nicobar Islands in Andaman & Nicobar?
source.a: Nicobari community dance
source.exp: Andaman & Nicobar is associated with Nicobari community dance. Nicobari community dances are accompanied by singing and express island customs and folklore. Lava belongs especially to Minicoy in Lakshadweep, so it is not the correct regional identification for the Nicobar Islands; the two Union Territories are geographically and culturally distinct.

edits.before: Chhau appears under Bihar, Jharkhand AND West Bengal — a multi-state overlap frequently tested.
edits.after: Chhau traditions: Seraikella in Jharkhand, Purulia in West Bengal and Mayurbhanj in Odisha.

source.q: In which three states does the Chhau dance appear?
source.a: Jharkhand (Seraikella), West Bengal (Purulia) and Odisha (Mayurbhanj)
source.exp: Chhau’s three principal styles are Seraikella in Jharkhand, Purulia in West Bengal and Mayurbhanj in Odisha. Seraikella and Purulia use masks, while Mayurbhanj generally does not; the modern three-state identification must include Odisha, not substitute Bihar.

edits.after: Ghumar DanceBhil women and other Rajasthani communitiesRajasthan

source.q: Ghoomar (Ghumar) is especially associated with which state and with the women of which traditionally linked community?
source.a: Rajasthan; Bhil women, alongside other Rajasthani communities
source.exp: Ghoomar is a well-known Rajasthani women’s dance performed by Bhil women and other communities, including Rajputs. Its circular movement and whirling skirts are characteristic; listing only the other states where Bhils live would miss the dance’s principal Rajasthan association.

edits.after: Karma DanceOraon, Munda, Gond and other communitiesCentral and eastern India

source.q: Which statement correctly describes the communities and region associated with Karma dance?
source.a: Several communities, including Oraon, Munda and Gond, across central and eastern India
source.exp: Karma or Karam dance is associated with the Karam festival and several central and eastern Indian communities, including Oraon, Munda and Gond groups. Karma is the name of a ritual and dance tradition, not evidence of a distinct “Karma tribe”; local forms vary.

edits.after: Sarhul DanceOraon, Munda and other communitiesJharkhand

source.q: The spring Sarhul festival and its community dances are strongly associated with which state and communities?
source.a: Jharkhand; Oraon and Munda communities, among others
source.exp: Sarhul is a spring festival of nature and village deities, prominently celebrated by Oraon, Munda and other communities in Jharkhand. Sal blossoms, music and community dancing are important; it is a festival context containing dances, not one universal dance choreography of a single tribe.

edits.before: Uttar PradeshKalgiturra, Phaag, Goulan Geet, Hid Gayan, Alha Gayan, Deori Geet, Bambuliya Geet, Vasdev, Birha, Videsiya
edits.after: Uttar PradeshAlha, Birha, Kajri, Chaiti and Phaag

source.q: Which of the following are folk songs of Uttar Pradesh?
source.a: Alha, Birha, Kajri, Chaiti and Phaag
source.exp: Alha narrates heroic stories, Birha expresses separation and related social themes, Kajri is associated with the rainy season, and Chaiti with Chaitra. These are prominent in Uttar Pradesh and neighbouring Hindi-speaking regions; Bidesia is especially associated with Bihar’s folk theatre.

edits.before: ChhattisgarhSohar, Kaherva, Chanaini, Nouwa Jhokkad, Banjarwa-Nayakwa, Kajli/Kajri, Jarewa-Parewa, Sadavraj Saranga
edits.after: ChhattisgarhDadaria, Sua songs, Sohar and Karma songs

source.q: Which of the following are folk songs of Chhattisgarh?
source.a: Dadaria, Sua songs, Sohar and Karma songs
source.exp: Dadaria is a well-known Chhattisgarhi folk-song tradition, while Sua and Karma songs accompany community or ritual performances. Sohar is sung around childbirth across several Hindi-speaking regions; shared traditions should not be presented as exclusive to Chhattisgarh.

edits.before: UttarakhandJhora, Chanchari, Bhagnaul, Bair, Rituren, Handukiya Bol, Malusahi, Jagar, Bhadoun, Shakunakshar (Fag)
edits.after: UttarakhandJhoda, Chanchari, Bhagnaul and Jagar

source.q: Which group belongs to Uttarakhand’s folk singing and song-dance traditions?
source.a: Jhoda, Chanchari, Bhagnaul and Jagar
source.exp: Jhoda and Chanchari combine group singing and dancing in Uttarakhand, while Bhagnaul is a folk singing tradition. Jagar invokes deities through ritual music and narrative; these names include song-dance and ritual genres, not only standalone songs.

edits.before: Chhattisgarh / MPBhojali, Pandavani, Jas, Bharthari, Bans geet, Gaura-Gauri song, Dewar song, Karma song
edits.after: Chhattisgarh / MPBhojali, Pandavani, Bharthari and Karma songs

source.q: Which of the following are folk songs of Chhattisgarh / MP?
source.a: Bhojali, Pandavani, Bharthari and Karma songs
source.exp: Pandavani narrates Mahabharata episodes, and Bharthari recounts the king-renouncer’s story. Bhojali and Karma songs have seasonal and ritual associations; these traditions are found especially in Chhattisgarh and related central Indian areas, with local variation.

edits.before: Bihar / JharkhandNanchari, Samdani, Jhumar, Tirhuti, Syam Chakeva, Chhath Songs, Jat-Jatin, Bargamani, Sohar
edits.after: Bihar / JharkhandNachari, Jhumar, Chhath songs, Jat-Jatin and Sohar

source.q: Which group belongs to Bihar and Jharkhand’s folk singing or song-dance traditions?
source.a: Nachari, Jhumar, Chhath songs, Jat-Jatin and Sohar
source.exp: Nachari songs belong to the Maithili devotional tradition, Chhath songs honour the Sun and Chhathi Maiya, and Sohar marks childbirth. Jat-Jatin and Jhumar can combine singing with dance; Bihar and Jharkhand’s repertoires overlap with neighbouring regions.

edits.before: RajasthanHalra, Kaman, Aalun-Jalo songs, Gangaur, Pankhida, Maud
edits.after: RajasthanHalar, Kaman, Gangaur songs, Panihari and Maand

source.q: Which of the following are folk songs of Rajasthan?
source.a: Halar, Kaman, Gangaur songs, Panihari and Maand
source.exp: Maand is a distinctive Rajasthani singing style; Panihari songs evoke women’s water-fetching lives. Gangaur songs accompany the festival, while Halar and Kaman relate to life-cycle and love themes; Maand should not be misspelt as “Maud”.

edits.after: AssamBihu songs, Assamese Lokgeet and Tokari geet

source.q: Which of the following are folk songs of Assam?
source.a: Bihu songs, Assamese Lokgeet and Tokari geet
source.exp: Bihu songs accompany Assam’s seasonal celebrations, and Tokari geet is sung with the tokari string instrument. Lokgeet means folk song broadly; it is not a single exclusive composition or the name of a distinct festival.

edits.after: KarnatakaJanapada Geethe, Sobane Pada and Tripadi songs

source.q: Which of the following are folk songs of Karnataka?
source.a: Janapada Geethe, Sobane Pada and Tripadi songs
source.exp: Karnataka’s Janapada Geethe encompasses folk songs, Sobane Pada is associated with auspicious domestic and wedding occasions, and Tripadi uses three-line verse. Dollu Kunitha and Veeragase are dance forms, so they do not belong in a list consisting only of folk songs.

edits.after: MaharashtraLavani, Powada, Ovi and Bhaleri

source.q: Which of the following are folk songs of Maharashtra?
source.a: Lavani, Powada, Ovi and Bhaleri
source.exp: Maharashtra’s Lavani combines rhythmic song and performance, Powada recounts heroic deeds, and Ovi is associated with everyday work and women’s oral traditions. Bhaleri songs have agricultural associations; the genres differ in purpose and setting.

edits.after: West BengalBaul, Bhatiyali and Bhawaiya

source.q: Which of the following are folk songs of West Bengal?
source.a: Baul, Bhatiyali and Bhawaiya
source.exp: Baul expresses spiritual ideas through song, Bhatiyali is associated with river and boatmen’s traditions, and Bhawaiya with northern Bengal’s rural life. These traditions extend across Bengal and neighbouring regions, including Bangladesh, rather than stopping at West Bengal’s border.

edits.after: KeralaVadakkan Pattu, Thekkan Pattu and Vanchipattu

source.q: Which of the following are folk songs of Kerala?
source.a: Vadakkan Pattu, Thekkan Pattu and Vanchipattu
source.exp: Kerala’s Vadakkan Pattu and Thekkan Pattu are northern and southern Malayalam ballad traditions; Vanchipattu is boat-song singing. Ballads recount heroes and local narratives, while boat songs coordinate collective singing and movement; these are named musical genres rather than community labels.

edits.after: ManipurPena Ishei and Khullong Ishei

source.q: Which of the following are folk songs of Manipur?
source.a: Pena Ishei and Khullong Ishei
source.exp: Pena Ishei is associated with singing to the pena, a traditional bowed instrument of Manipur, and Khullong Ishei belongs to regional folk singing. Baul belongs chiefly to the Bengal cultural region, while Phungawari is storytelling; those cannot all be labelled Manipuri folk songs.

edits.after: Arunachal PradeshJa-Jin-Ja, Baryi and Nyioga

source.q: Which of the following are folk songs of Arunachal Pradesh?
source.a: Ja-Jin-Ja, Baryi and Nyioga
source.exp: Ja-Jin-Ja, Baryi and Nyioga are song traditions associated with Arunachal Pradesh, particularly Pailibo cultural accounts. They relate to social occasions, ancestral or religious narrative and weddings; local-language names have varying Roman transliterations.

edits.after: NagalandLi songs of the Chakhesang/Chokri tradition and other Naga community songs

source.q: Which of the following are folk songs of Nagaland?
source.a: Li songs of the Chakhesang/Chokri tradition and other Naga community songs
source.exp: Li is a folk-song tradition of the Chakhesang/Chokri cultural region of Nagaland. Naga communities also preserve agricultural, celebratory and historical songs through oral transmission; Nagaland’s many tribes do not share just one uniform repertoire.

edits.after: Jammu & KashmirWanwun

source.q: Which of the following is a folk song of Jammu & Kashmir?
source.a: Wanwun
source.exp: Wanwun is traditional Kashmiri ceremonial singing, especially associated with weddings and other auspicious occasions. It is often performed collectively; the spelling “Vanabun” obscures the recognised name and should not be treated as a different song form.

edits.before: HoliFull moon day of Falgun (Spring); Lathmar Holi next day after Holika Dahan
edits.after: HoliHoli season around Phalguna Purnima; Lathmar Holi is the pre-main-Holi stick-and-shield tradition of Barsana and Nandgaon

source.q: When is Holi celebrated, and what is Lathmar Holi?
source.a: Holi season around Phalguna Purnima; Lathmar Holi is the pre-main-Holi stick-and-shield tradition of Barsana and Nandgaon
source.exp: Holika Dahan is observed on Phalguna Purnima, with the main colour-playing celebration generally on the following day. Lathmar Holi in Barsana and Nandgaon takes place earlier in the Braj Holi season, with women playfully using sticks and men defending with shields; it is not simply the day after Holika Dahan.

edits.before: Vijayadashami10th day of Shukla Paksha, Ashwin; symbol of Rama's victory over Ravana
edits.after: Vijayadashami10th day of Shukla Paksha, Ashwin; symbolizes Rama's victory over Ravana

source.q: When is Vijayadashami celebrated, and what does it symbolize?
source.a: 10th day of Shukla Paksha, Ashwin; symbolizes Rama's victory over Ravana
source.exp: Vijayadashami falls on Ashvina Shukla Dashami, following the nine nights of Navratri. Rama’s victory over Ravana and Durga’s victory over Mahishasura are major associated traditions, symbolising the triumph of good over evil rather than one exclusive regional narrative.

edits.before: JanmashtamiAshtami of Krishna Paksha, Bhadrapada; birthday of Lord Krishna
edits.after: JanmashtamiAshtami of Krishna Paksha, Bhadrapada — Lord Krishna's birthday

source.q: In the North Indian purnimanta calendar, when is Janmashtami observed?
source.a: Ashtami of Krishna Paksha, Bhadrapada — Lord Krishna's birthday
source.exp: Janmashtami commemorates Krishna’s birth on Krishna Paksha Ashtami, called Bhadrapada in the North Indian purnimanta calendar. In some amanta calendars the same fortnight is labelled Shravana; fasting and midnight worship are common, and exact civil dates can vary with calendrical rules.

edits.before: Ramnavami9th day of Shukla Paksha, Chaitra; birthday of Lord Rama
edits.after: Ramnavami9th day of Shukla Paksha, Chaitra — Lord Rama's birthday

source.q: When is Ramnavami celebrated?
source.a: 9th day of Shukla Paksha, Chaitra — Lord Rama's birthday
source.exp: Rama Navami commemorates the birth of Rama on Chaitra Shukla Navami. It falls within spring Navratri and is distinct from Vijayadashami, which commemorates victory traditions in the autumn month of Ashvina.

edits.before: Basant Panchami5th day of Shukla Paksha, Magh; worship of Goddess Saraswati
edits.after: Basant Panchami5th day of Shukla Paksha, Magh — Goddess Saraswati's worship

source.q: When is Basant Panchami celebrated, and which goddess is worshipped?
source.a: 5th day of Shukla Paksha, Magh — Goddess Saraswati's worship
source.exp: Basant Panchami falls on Magha Shukla Panchami and is closely associated with Saraswati, the goddess of learning, music and arts. It welcomes the spring season in many regions, where yellow clothes, educational rituals and cultural activities are common.

edits.before: Raksha BandhanFull moon of Shravan; bond between brother and sister
edits.after: Raksha BandhanFull moon of Shravan — brother-sister bond

source.q: When is Raksha Bandhan celebrated?
source.a: Full moon of Shravan — brother-sister bond
source.exp: Raksha Bandhan is observed on Shravana Purnima, usually in August. Tying a rakhi expresses affection and mutual care, especially between siblings; the date is lunar, so it is not fixed to one Gregorian day every year.

edits.before: Ganesh ChaturthiChaturthi of Shukla Paksha, Bhadrapada; started by Balgangadhar Tilak
edits.after: Ganesh ChaturthiBhadrapada Shukla Chaturthi; Bal Gangadhar Tilak popularised public celebrations in 1893

source.q: When is Ganesh Chaturthi observed, and who popularised its large-scale public celebration in 1893?
source.a: Bhadrapada Shukla Chaturthi; Bal Gangadhar Tilak popularised public celebrations in 1893
source.exp: Ganesh Chaturthi begins on Bhadrapada Shukla Chaturthi. Tilak popularised large-scale public Ganesh celebrations in 1893 to foster social unity and nationalist mobilisation; Ganesha worship and earlier local public celebrations predated him.

edits.after: Makar SankrantiSun God

source.q: To whom is Makar Sankranti dedicated?
source.a: Sun God
source.exp: Makar Sankranti marks the Sun’s entry into Makara in the traditional sidereal zodiac and honours Surya. Usually falling around 14–15 January, it is a solar festival associated with harvest, ritual bathing and regional celebrations such as Uttarayan and Thai Pongal.

edits.before: Gyan PanchamiJyeshtha Shukla Panchami; Jain scriptures written & worshipped

source.q: When is Mahavir Jayanti celebrated?
source.a: 13th of Shukla Paksha, Chaitra — Lord Mahavir's birthday
source.exp: Mahavir Jayanti falls on Chaitra Shukla Trayodashi and commemorates Mahavira, the twenty-fourth Jain Tirthankara. It is a birth celebration, distinct from the Jain Diwali association with Mahavira’s nirvana.

edits.before: Eid-ul-FitrFirst day of Shawwal, after Ramadan ends
edits.after: Eid-ul-FitrFirst day of Shawwal, after the end of Ramadan

source.q: When is Eid-ul-Fitr celebrated?
source.a: First day of Shawwal, after the end of Ramadan
source.exp: Eid-ul-Fitr falls on 1 Shawwal, the tenth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, immediately after Ramadan fasting ends. Communal prayer, charity and sharing food are central; local moon-sighting practice can produce different civil dates in different countries.

edits.before: Eid-ul-Adha (Bakrid)10th of Hajj month; memory of Prophet Ibrahim's sacrifice
edits.after: Eid-ul-Adha (Bakrid)10 Dhu al-Hijjah; commemorates Ibrahim’s willingness to sacrifice in obedience to God

source.q: When is Eid-ul-Adha / Bakrid celebrated, and what is its significance?
source.a: 10 Dhu al-Hijjah; commemorates Ibrahim’s willingness to sacrifice in obedience to God
source.exp: Eid-ul-Adha begins on 10 Dhu al-Hijjah, the Islamic calendar’s final month, during the Hajj season. It commemorates Ibrahim’s readiness to obey God’s command; sacrifice and sharing with relatives and those in need express its devotional and charitable meaning.

edits.before: MuharramFestival of mourning; first holy month of Islamic calendar
edits.after: MuharramThe first Islamic month; Ashura on its tenth day includes remembrance of Karbala, especially among Shia Muslims

source.q: What is Muharram?
source.a: The first Islamic month; Ashura on its tenth day includes remembrance of Karbala, especially among Shia Muslims
source.exp: Muharram is the first month of the Islamic calendar and one of its sacred months, not simply the name of a festival. Ashura is its tenth day; Shia Muslims particularly mourn Husayn’s death at Karbala, while Sunni observances also include fasting with other historical associations.

edits.before: Vaisakhi1st Vaishakh (April-May); founding of Khalsa Panth by Guru Gobind Singh
edits.after: VaisakhiFirst day of the solar month Vaisakh, around 13–14 April; Khalsa founded by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699

source.q: When is Vaisakhi celebrated, and what is its significance?
source.a: First day of the solar month Vaisakh, around 13–14 April; Khalsa founded by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699
source.exp: Vaisakhi marks the start of the solar month Vaisakh and a major Punjabi harvest celebration, normally around 13–14 April. In Sikh history it commemorates Guru Gobind Singh’s creation of the Khalsa at Anandpur Sahib in 1699; the Vaisakhi festival itself was older.

edits.before: Hola MohallaDay after Holi; started by Guru Gobind Singh
edits.after: Hola MohallaAround Holi, especially at Anandpur Sahib; instituted by Guru Gobind Singh in 1701

source.q: When is Hola Mohalla celebrated, and who started it?
source.a: Around Holi, especially at Anandpur Sahib; instituted by Guru Gobind Singh in 1701
source.exp: Guru Gobind Singh instituted Hola Mohalla at Anandpur Sahib in 1701, linking the Holi season with martial preparedness and community gathering. It features displays of skill, processions, devotional music and langar; present celebrations extend across several days rather than one universally fixed day after Holi.

edits.after: Christmas25 December — birth of Jesus Christ

source.q: On which Gregorian date do most Western Christian churches celebrate Christmas?
source.a: 25 December — birth of Jesus Christ
source.exp: Most Western churches celebrate Jesus Christ’s birth at Christmas on 25 December in the Gregorian calendar. Some Eastern churches retain 25 December in the Julian calendar, currently corresponding to 7 January Gregorian; the feast date is not a historically verified birth date.

edits.after: NavrozAround the March equinox, conventionally 21 March

source.q: When is the spring-equinox celebration Jamshedi Navroz observed?
source.a: Around the March equinox, conventionally 21 March
source.exp: Jamshedi Navroz is the spring-equinox celebration conventionally associated with 21 March. It must be distinguished from New Year under the un-intercalated Shahenshahi Parsi calendar, which currently falls in August; “Parsi New Year” therefore does not imply one date for every calendar tradition.

edits.before: Khordad SalBirthday of Zarathust, founder of Parsis
edits.after: Khordad SalThe traditional birthday celebration of Zarathustra (Zoroaster), prophet of Zoroastrianism

source.q: What is Khordad Sal?
source.a: The traditional birthday celebration of Zarathustra (Zoroaster), prophet of Zoroastrianism
source.exp: Khordad Sal celebrates the traditional birthday of Zarathustra, the prophet associated with Zoroastrianism. Parsis are an Indian Zoroastrian community, not a religion personally founded as “Parsis” by him; observance dates differ among Zoroastrian calendar systems.

edits.after: PongalTamil NaduTamil Nadu; four-day harvest season celebration around mid-January, with Thai Pongal around 14–15 January

source.q: Where and when is Pongal celebrated?
source.a: Tamil Nadu; four-day harvest season celebration around mid-January, with Thai Pongal around 14–15 January
source.exp: Pongal is Tamil Nadu’s harvest celebration, comprising Bhogi, Thai Pongal, Mattu Pongal and Kaanum Pongal. Thai Pongal marks the start of the Tamil month Thai around 14–15 January; Bhogi precedes it, so the whole four-day sequence cannot always be said to start on 14 January.

edits.before: OnamKeralaHarvest festival; boat race; started by Chera king Mahabali
edits.after: OnamKeralaHarvest festivities; legendary return of King Mahabali

source.q: Where is Onam celebrated, and what is its significance?
source.a: Kerala; harvest festivities and the legendary return of King Mahabali
source.exp: Onam is Kerala’s major festival in the Malayalam month Chingam, linked to harvest and the legendary annual return of Mahabali. Floral pookalam, communal meals and boat-race traditions feature prominently; Mahabali is a mythological king, not an established historical Chera ruler.

edits.before: ChhathBihar (most famous), Eastern UPShashthi of Shukla Paksha, Kartik; worship of the Sun
edits.after: ChhathBihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar PradeshKartika Shukla Shashthi; honours the Sun and Chhathi Maiya

source.q: Where is Chhath most famous, and when is it celebrated?
source.a: Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh; main Kartika observance centred on Shukla Shashthi, honouring the Sun and Chhathi Maiya
source.exp: Chhath is especially important in Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh. Its four-day Kartika observance includes offerings to the setting and rising Sun around Shukla Shashthi; Chhathi Maiya is also worshipped, and a spring Chaiti Chhath occurs in Chaitra.

edits.after: Mysore DussehraKarnatakaWodeyar royal observance begun by Raja Wodeyar I at Srirangapatna in 1610

source.q: Which state hosts Mysuru Dasara, and when did Raja Wodeyar I begin the Wodeyar royal observance at Srirangapatna?
source.a: Karnataka; 1610
source.exp: Mysuru Dasara is Karnataka’s state festival, rooted in older South Indian royal Navratri traditions. Raja Wodeyar I began the Wodeyar observance at Srirangapatna in 1610; the broader Vijayanagara background must be distinguished from that specific dynastic beginning.

edits.before: dedicated to the Sun God and his wife Usha
edits.after: honouring the Sun and Chhathi Maiya

source.q: Where is Chhath most famous, and when is it celebrated?
source.a: Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh; main Kartika observance centred on Shukla Shashthi, honouring the Sun and Chhathi Maiya
source.exp: Chhath is especially important in Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh. Its four-day Kartika observance includes offerings to the setting and rising Sun around Shukla Shashthi; Chhathi Maiya is also worshipped, and a spring Chaiti Chhath occurs in Chaitra.

edits.before: Pushkar Camel FairRajasthan; world's largest camel fair
edits.after: Pushkar Camel FairPushkar, Rajasthan; a major annual camel and livestock fair around Kartika Purnima

source.q: Where is the Pushkar Camel Fair held, and what is its significance?
source.a: Pushkar, Rajasthan; a major annual camel and livestock fair around Kartika Purnima
source.exp: Pushkar’s annual fair combines camel and other livestock trading, cultural performances and pilgrimage around Kartika Purnima. It is among the best-known large camel fairs; an absolute “world’s largest” ranking requires a specified year and metric, so its location and character provide a more stable fact.

edits.after: Pushkar Camel FairPushkar, Rajasthan; a major annual camel and livestock fair around Kartika Purnima

source.q: Where is the Pushkar Camel Fair held, and what is its significance?
source.a: Pushkar, Rajasthan; a major annual camel and livestock fair around Kartika Purnima
source.exp: Pushkar’s annual fair combines camel and other livestock trading, cultural performances and pilgrimage around Kartika Purnima. It is among the best-known large camel fairs; an absolute “world’s largest” ranking requires a specified year and metric, so its location and character provide a more stable fact.

edits.before: Bahu FairJammu; one of biggest Hindu festivals
edits.after: Bahu FairJammu; a devotional fair at Bahu Fort’s Bawe Wali Mata temple during Navratri

source.q: Where is the Bahu Fair held, and what is its significance?
source.a: Jammu; a devotional fair at Bahu Fort’s Bawe Wali Mata temple during Navratri
source.exp: Bahu Mela is held at the Kali temple known as Bawe Wali Mata within Bahu Fort in Jammu. It is associated with spring and autumn Navratri gatherings; this specific regional devotional identity is clearer than an unsupported national ranking of festival size.

edits.before: Sonpur Cattle FairSonpur (Bihar); Asia's largest, at Ganga-Gandak confluence
edits.after: Sonpur Cattle FairSonepur, Bihar; a historic major cattle and cultural fair near the Ganga–Gandak confluence

source.q: Where is the Sonpur Cattle Fair held, and what is its significance?
source.a: Sonepur, Bihar; a historic major cattle and cultural fair near the Ganga–Gandak confluence
source.exp: Sonepur’s Harihar Kshetra Mela in Bihar begins around Kartika Purnima near the Ganga–Gandak confluence. It has a long history of animal trading, pilgrimage and cultural activity; its historical fame as a very large cattle fair should not be mistaken for a measured, permanent current ranking.

edits.after: Shehnai – Bharat RatnaUstad Bismillah Khan

source.q: Shehnai — Bharat Ratna (2001)?
source.a: Ustad Bismillah Khan
source.exp: Bismillah Khan brought the shehnai, a double-reed wind instrument, to prominence on the Hindustani concert stage. He received the Bharat Ratna in 2001, the same award year as singer Lata Mangeshkar; she was not a shehnai player.

edits.after: Total Classical DancesEight

source.q: How many forms are in the standard recognised list of Indian classical dances?
source.a: Eight
source.exp: The standard eight are Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Odissi and Sattriya. Chhau is a major eastern Indian dance tradition inscribed as UNESCO intangible heritage in 2010; international heritage listing and domestic classical-dance classification are different systems.

edits.before: Bharatanatyam"5th Veda"; Tamil Nadu; banned 1910, later revived
edits.after: BharatanatyamTamil Nadu; roots in Sadir and a twentieth-century revival

source.q: Bharatanatyam?
source.a: Tamil Nadu; roots in Sadir and a twentieth-century revival
source.exp: Bharatanatyam developed from Sadir traditions sustained by hereditary performers in Tamil temple and court settings. Devadasis were important custodians, but there was no single universally documented “last devadasi” for all India; modern reformulation involved both hereditary artists and revivalists.

edits.before: KuchipudiAndhra Pradesh; founded by Siddhendra Yogi; concludes with Tarangam
edits.after: KuchipudiAndhra Pradesh; Siddhendra Yogi tradition and the characteristic Tarangam item

source.q: Kuchipudi?
source.a: Andhra Pradesh; Siddhendra Yogi tradition and the characteristic Tarangam item
source.exp: Kuchipudi developed in Andhra Pradesh, with Siddhendra Yogi traditionally credited with shaping its devotional dance-drama. Tarangam is a characteristic item in which the dancer performs on the rim of a brass plate; it need not conclude every programme, and the tradition also has solo presentations.

edits.before: KathakaliKerala; oldest theatrical dance style; Kalamandalam est. 1930
edits.after: KathakaliKerala; stylised dance-drama, supported by Kerala Kalamandalam founded in 1930

source.q: Kathakali?
source.a: Kerala; stylised dance-drama, supported by Kerala Kalamandalam founded in 1930
source.exp: Kathakali is Kerala’s stylised dance-drama, developing prominently from the seventeenth century and drawing on older performance traditions. Kerala Kalamandalam, founded in 1930 by Vallathol Narayana Menon and Manakkulam Mukunda Raja, helped its revival; older Kerala theatre such as Kutiyattam makes “oldest theatrical style” an inaccurate absolute description.

edits.before: ManipuriManipur; based on Raasleela of Radha and Krishna
edits.after: ManipuriManipur; Radha-Krishna Ras and other Meitei ritual and percussion-dance traditions

source.q: Manipuri?
source.a: Manipur; Radha-Krishna Ras and other Meitei ritual and percussion-dance traditions
source.exp: Manipuri developed in Manipur, drawing on Meitei ritual traditions as well as later Vaishnava devotion. Its Ras dances portray Radha and Krishna, but the wider repertoire also includes Lai Haraoba and percussion dances; a language is not the geographical origin of a dance.

edits.before: OdissiOdisha; evidence in Udayagiri caves (2nd century BCE)
edits.after: OdissiOdisha; Mahari and Gotipua roots, with ancient dance evidence at Udayagiri–Khandagiri

source.q: Odissi?
source.a: Odisha; Mahari and Gotipua roots, with ancient dance evidence at Udayagiri–Khandagiri
source.exp: Odissi draws on temple Mahari dancers, Gotipua performers and regional artistic traditions. Udayagiri–Khandagiri’s first-century-BCE remains associated with Kharavela show early dance culture; they are not proof that today’s complete Odissi repertoire already existed unchanged at that date.

edits.after: KathakNorth India, including major Uttar Pradesh centres; name derived from katha (story)

source.q: Kathak?
source.a: North India, including major Uttar Pradesh centres; name derived from katha (story)
source.exp: Kathak derives from katha, meaning story, and the kathak or storyteller tradition. Leila Sokhey, known as Madame Menaka, helped promote it through stage productions and touring; its modern development also depended on hereditary gharana artists, not one revivalist alone.

edits.after: Chhau (UNESCO)Seraikella (Jharkhand), Purulia (West Bengal), Mayurbhanj (Odisha); UNESCO intangible heritage inscription in 2010

source.q: Chhau (UNESCO)?
source.a: Seraikella (Jharkhand), Purulia (West Bengal), Mayurbhanj (Odisha); UNESCO intangible heritage inscription in 2010
source.exp: Chhau was inscribed as UNESCO intangible cultural heritage in 2010. Its principal styles are Seraikella in Jharkhand, Purulia in West Bengal and Mayurbhanj in Odisha; the first two use masks, while Mayurbhanj generally does not, distinguishing the shared tradition’s regional forms.

edits.before: Kumbh MelaEvery 12 years; 4 locations: Haridwar, Prayagraj, Nasik, Ujjain
edits.after: Kumbh MelaAbout twelve years at each site; Haridwar, Prayagraj, Nashik–Trimbakeshwar and Ujjain

source.q: Kumbh Mela?
source.a: About twelve years at each site; Haridwar, Prayagraj, Nashik–Trimbakeshwar and Ujjain
source.exp: Full Kumbh gatherings recur at each of four principal sites on an approximately twelve-year astrological cycle. Events at different sites occur in different years, and Ardh Kumbh is associated with six-year intervals at Prayagraj and Haridwar; it is therefore wrong to infer a twelve-year gap between all Kumbh events worldwide.

edits.before: OnamKerala; harvest festival; boat race; by Chera king Mahabali
edits.after: OnamKerala; harvest festivities and the legendary return of King Mahabali

source.q: Onam?
source.a: Kerala; harvest festivities and the legendary return of King Mahabali
source.exp: Onam is Kerala’s major festival in the Malayalam month Chingam, linked to harvest and the legendary annual return of Mahabali. Floral pookalam, communal meals and boat-race traditions feature prominently; Mahabali is a mythological king, not an established historical Chera ruler.

source.exp: Pongal is Tamil Nadu’s harvest celebration, comprising Bhogi, Thai Pongal, Mattu Pongal and Kaanum Pongal. Thai Pongal marks the start of the Tamil month Thai around 14–15 January; Bhogi precedes it, so the whole four-day sequence cannot always be said to start on 14 January.

edits.after: Chhath PujaEspecially Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh; worship of Surya and Chhathi Maiya

source.q: Chhath Puja?
source.a: Especially Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh; worship of Surya and Chhathi Maiya
source.exp: Chhath is especially important in Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh. Its four-day Kartika observance includes offerings to the setting and rising Sun around Shukla Shashthi; Chhathi Maiya is also worshipped, and a spring Chaiti Chhath occurs in Chaitra.

edits.after: Gandhi Jayanti2 October; Gandhi’s birthday and the International Day of Non-Violence

source.q: Gandhi Jayanti?
source.a: 2 October; Gandhi’s birthday and the International Day of Non-Violence
source.exp: Gandhi Jayanti marks Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi’s birth on 2 October 1869. The United Nations observes 2 October as the International Day of Non-Violence; 30 January instead commemorates Gandhi’s assassination in 1948.

edits.after: Ghatam virtuoso “Vikku”

source.q: Which ghatam virtuoso is known as “Vikku” Vinayakram?
source.a: T.H. Vinayakram
source.exp: T.H. “Vikku” Vinayakram is a celebrated Carnatic ghatam artist. The ghatam is a clay pot played by striking its body and mouth with the hands; the pot itself vibrates, placing it among solid-body ghana instruments rather than membrane drums.

edits.after: AIDSAcquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome

source.q: What is the full form of AIDS?
source.a: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome
source.exp: AIDS stands for Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome. It is the most advanced stage of HIV infection, in which the immune system is severely weakened. HIV is the virus; AIDS is a syndrome caused by advanced infection, not the name of that virus.

edits.before: ASSOCHAMAssociated Chambers of Commerce and Industry
edits.after: ASSOCHAMAssociated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India

source.q: What is the full form of ASSOCHAM?
source.a: Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India
source.exp: ASSOCHAM stands for Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India. It is an Indian apex business chamber representing commerce and industry and contributing to policy discussions. The complete institutional name includes “of India”; ASSOCHAM is not a government ministry.

edits.before: AWACSAirborne Warning and Aircraft Control System
edits.after: AWACSAirborne Warning and Control System

source.q: What is the full form of AWACS?
source.a: Airborne Warning and Control System
source.exp: AWACS stands for Airborne Warning and Control System. These aircraft-based systems provide radar surveillance, early warning and command-and-control support for air operations. The standard expansion does not insert the extra word “Aircraft” between “and” and “Control”.

edits.after: CSOCentral Statistics Office

source.q: In Indian official statistics before the 2019 restructuring, what did CSO stand for?
source.a: Central Statistics Office
source.exp: CSO stands for Central Statistics Office. Before the 2019 restructuring, CSO’s Office-era name was Central Statistics Office. The older name was Central Statistical Organisation; CSO and NSSO were brought into the National Statistical Office framework, so the vague claim “now Office” is insufficient.

edits.after: CTBTComprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty

source.q: What is the full form of CTBT?
source.a: Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty
source.exp: CTBT stands for Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty. This treaty was adopted in 1996 and provides for banning nuclear explosions in all environments. “Nuclear” is part of the full title; the treaty’s adoption must not be confused with its entry into force.

edits.after: FERAForeign Exchange Regulation Act — repealed

source.q: What is the full form of FERA, and what is its current status?
source.a: Foreign Exchange Regulation Act — repealed
source.exp: FERA was the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973. It was repealed when FEMA became effective on 1 June 2000; repeal does not mean that all legal consequences of older violations automatically disappeared.

edits.after: FEMAForeign Exchange Management Act — effective from 1 June 2000

source.q: What is the full form of FEMA, and when did it replace FERA?
source.a: Foreign Exchange Management Act — effective from 1 June 2000
source.exp: FEMA is the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999: 1999 identifies the enactment year. It came into force and replaced FERA on 1 June 2000, with the objective of facilitating external trade and payments and orderly foreign-exchange-market development.

edits.before: GATTGeneral Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
edits.after: GATTGeneral Agreement on Tariffs and Trade — predecessor to WTO

source.q: What is the full form of GATT, and what was it the predecessor to?
source.a: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade — predecessor to WTO
source.exp: GATT stands for General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade — predecessor to WTO. GATT provided the earlier multilateral trade framework, and the WTO succeeded that institutional framework on 1 January 1995. GATT did not simply vanish: the updated GATT 1994 remains part of the WTO agreements governing trade in goods.

edits.after: GSMGlobal System for Mobile Communications

source.q: What is the full form of GSM?
source.a: Global System for Mobile Communications
source.exp: GSM stands for Global System for Mobile Communications. GSM is a digital cellular standard associated with second-generation mobile networks. Its expanded English name uses the plural “Communications”; the acronym originated from the earlier French name Groupe Spécial Mobile.

edits.after: QMGQuartermaster General

source.q: What is the full form of QMG for the military logistics appointment?
source.a: Quartermaster General
source.exp: QMG stands for Quartermaster General. The Quartermaster General is a senior military logistics appointment associated with supplies, transport and related support. “Quartermaster” is conventionally one word; QMG is not a generic quality-management group in this context.

edits.after: SIMSubscriber Identity Module

source.q: What is the full form of SIM in mobile telecommunications?
source.a: Subscriber Identity Module
source.exp: SIM stands for Subscriber Identity Module. A SIM securely stores subscriber identity information and authentication credentials used by a mobile network. The standard name is Subscriber Identity Module, not Subscriber Identification Module; removable cards and embedded SIM arrangements can perform this role.

edits.after: SMSShort Message Service

source.q: What is the full form of SMS in mobile text messaging?
source.a: Short Message Service
source.exp: SMS stands for Short Message Service. SMS is the mobile-network service for short text messages. The standard expansion uses “Message”, not “Messaging”; this terminology is distinct from internet-based chat applications that may also send short messages.

edits.after: STDSubscriber Trunk Dialling

source.q: What is the full form of STD in long-distance telephony?
source.a: Subscriber Trunk Dialling
source.exp: STD stands for Subscriber Trunk Dialling. Subscriber Trunk Dialling enables a telephone subscriber to dial long-distance trunk calls without an operator placing the call. In medical usage STD has a different meaning, so the telephony context fixes this expansion.

edits.after: STEPSatellite Telecommunication Experiments Project

source.q: What is the full form of STEP in ISRO's 1977–1979 satellite communication experiment?
source.a: Satellite Telecommunication Experiments Project
source.exp: STEP stands for Satellite Telecommunication Experiments Project. STEP was the Satellite Telecommunication Experiments Project, undertaken by ISRO and the Posts and Telegraphs Department using the Franco-German Symphonie satellite during 1977–1979. The plural “Experiments” is part of this historical project’s name; it was not a launch vehicle.

edits.before: TADATerrorist and Disruptive Activities Prevention Act
edits.after: TADATerrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act

source.q: What is the full form of TADA for the historical Indian anti-terrorism law?
source.a: Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act
source.exp: TADA stands for Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act. TADA was the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, an Indian anti-terrorism law that lapsed in 1995. “Prevention” is the parenthetical word in the title; the historical Act must not be described as a currently operating general law.

edits.after: WWWWorld Wide Web

source.q: What is the full form of WWW?
source.a: World Wide Web
source.exp: WWW stands for World Wide Web. The World Wide Web is the system of linked web resources accessed using browsers and web protocols. It operates over the internet, but the web and the internet are not identical: the internet also carries services such as email.

edits.after: ZUPOZimbabwe United People's Organisation

source.q: What is the full form of ZUPO for the historical Rhodesian political party led by Jeremiah Chirau?
source.a: Zimbabwe United People's Organisation
source.exp: ZUPO stands for Zimbabwe United People's Organisation. ZUPO was a historical Rhodesian political party led by Chief Jeremiah Chirau during the transition towards Zimbabwe. “Zimbabwe United People’s Organisation” is the name; it must not be confused with ZAPU, Zimbabwe African People’s Union.

edits.after: FEMA was enacted in 1999 and became effective on 1 June 2000.

source.q: Without confusing FERA and FEMA, state the difference.
source.a: FERA — Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, repealed; FEMA — Foreign Exchange Management Act, effective from 1 June 2000
source.exp: FERA was the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973; FEMA is the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999. FEMA replaced FERA with effect from 1 June 2000: 1999 is the enactment year, while 2000 is the commencement year.

edits.after: the standard abbreviation of United Nations is UN.

source.q: Which statement correctly gives the conventional UNO expansion and the standard abbreviation of United Nations?
source.a: UNO — United Nations Organization; standard abbreviation — UN
source.exp: United Nations Organization is a conventional expansion of UNO, but the organisation’s official short name is United Nations, abbreviated UN. The distinction is between a familiar descriptive expansion and the institution’s standard short name, not a change in the organisation itself.

edits.after: VariableCommonwealth Day: second Monday in March

source.q: Under the present Commonwealth-wide calendar, when is Commonwealth Day observed?
source.a: The second Monday in March
source.exp: The present Commonwealth-wide observance is on the second Monday in March, so its calendar date changes each year; in 2026 it fell on 9 March. The older 24 May association comes from Empire Day and historical Commonwealth Day usage, not the current common date.

source.q: On which date does World Breastfeeding Week begin each year?
source.a: 1 August
source.exp: World Breastfeeding Week runs from 1 to 7 August each year, so its opening date is 1 August. Supported by WHO and UNICEF, it promotes environments that support breastfeeding; describing the entire observance as a single “World Breastfeeding Day” loses the official week-long distinction.

edits.before: 26National Law Day / Constitution Day / Guru Nanak Dev Jayanti
edits.after: 26National Law Day / Constitution Day

source.q: On which date are Constitution Day and the traditional Law Day observed in India?
source.a: 26 November
source.exp: Constitution Day and the traditional Law Day fall on 26 November in India, marking the Constitution’s adoption in 1949. Most of the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950. Guru Nanak Jayanti generally follows Kartik Purnima, so its Gregorian date varies and cannot be fixed permanently at 26 November.

edits.after: International Customs Day

source.q: On which date are India’s Republic Day and International Customs Day observed?
source.a: 26 January
source.exp: India’s Republic Day and International Customs Day are both observed on 26 January. Republic Day marks the Constitution’s commencement in 1950; Customs Day recalls the first session of the Customs Co-operation Council, now the World Customs Organization, on 26 January 1953.

edits.after: United Nations Day

source.q: When is United Nations Day, marking the entry into force of the UN Charter, observed?
source.a: 24 October
source.exp: United Nations Day is observed on 24 October, marking the UN Charter’s entry into force on 24 October 1945. The Charter had been signed on 26 June 1945, but the organisation formally came into existence when the required ratifications were completed in October.

edits.after: National Consumer Day

source.q: When is National Consumer Day observed in India?
source.a: 24 December
source.exp: India’s National Consumer Day is observed on 24 December, the date when the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 received presidential assent. The newer Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replaced that law, but the commemorative date remains 24 December; World Consumer Rights Day is on 15 March.

edits.after: Rotary World Understanding and Peace Day

source.q: When does Rotary observe World Understanding and Peace Day?
source.a: 23 February
source.exp: Rotary observes World Understanding and Peace Day on 23 February, its founding anniversary. The first Rotary club was founded in Chicago on 23 February 1905; this Rotary-linked observance is distinct from the UN International Day of Peace on 21 September.

edits.after: Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy's birth and death anniversary

source.q: When is National Doctors' Day observed in India, and whom does it commemorate?
source.a: 1 July — Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy’s birth and death anniversaries
source.exp: India’s National Doctors’ Day is observed on 1 July in memory of Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy, physician and former Chief Minister of West Bengal. He was born on 1 July 1882 and died on 1 July 1962, so the date marks both his birth and death anniversaries.

source.q: Which listed UN initiative has the designated period 2022–2032?
source.a: International Decade of Indigenous Languages
source.exp: The International Decade of Indigenous Languages is 2022–2032, not 2021–2032. It promotes the preservation, revitalisation and use of Indigenous languages and recognises their importance to cultural identity, traditional knowledge and the rights of their speakers.

edits.after: 2016–2025, extended to 2030

source.q: Which UN initiative originally covered 2016–2025 and was extended to 2030?
source.a: United Nations Decade of Action on Nutrition
source.exp: The United Nations Decade of Action on Nutrition was originally proclaimed for 2016–2025 and was extended to 2030 in March 2025. It addresses malnutrition in all its forms through healthier food systems and coordinated policies; 2016–2025 remains its original period, not its current endpoint.

edits.before: Third UN Decade for the Eradication of Poverty
edits.after: Third UN Decade for the Eradication of Poverty (2018–2027)

source.q: The Third United Nations Decade for 2018–2027 was proclaimed for which objective?
source.a: Eradication of Poverty
source.exp: The Third United Nations Decade for the Eradication of Poverty covers 2018–2027. Its objective is poverty eradication through coordinated development action; “Third” refers to this particular series of poverty decades, not to every UN decade programme collectively.

edits.before: 2025International Year of Glaciers' Preservation / Quantum Science and Technology
edits.after: 2025International Year of Glaciers’ Preservation / International Year of Quantum Science and Technology

source.q: Which pair of UN International Year designations both belongs to 2025?
source.a: International Year of Glaciers’ Preservation / International Year of Quantum Science and Technology
source.exp: Both the International Year of Glaciers’ Preservation and the International Year of Quantum Science and Technology were designated for 2025. These were not the UN’s only designations for that year: 2025 was also the International Year of Cooperatives and the International Year of Peace and Trust.

edits.after: 2026International Year of the Woman Farmer

source.q: Which listed UN International Year designation belongs to 2026?
source.a: International Year of the Woman Farmer
source.exp: 2026 is the International Year of the Woman Farmer, recognising women’s contribution to agrifood systems and the inequalities they face. The official title uses “the Woman Farmer”; the UN can designate multiple International Years for the same calendar year, so this is not a single universal annual theme.
